Hi Sam  great questions, thanks for following up. High level answers below and I've attached a short POC plan that covers timelines, success criteria, and environment options (redwood-poc-plan.pdf).

1) Hosted vs Dedicated: For a 2-week exploratory trial focused on output quality, latency SLOs for single requests, and easy instrumenting, the hosted sandbox is usually sufficient. If you want to stress throughput (concurrent long-running sessions) or require network-isolated traffic (PHI), we'd recommend a short-lived Dedicated sandbox or VPC trial.

2) Suggested success criteria (sample):
  - Latency: p50 < 250ms and p95 < 800ms for our typical 512-token prompts
  - Cost: < $0.015 per 1k tokens for inference (target to be adjusted after initial week)
  - Quality: >= 90% pass on the 20-case eval prompt set (see attached prompts)
  - Security: No unapproved egress to external storage; audit logs enabled for all requests

Next steps I propose:
  - You confirm environment choice (hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial)
  - We lock success criteria and the 20-case eval set (I attached the eval in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1example)
  - Schedule a kickoff call for the week of Jul 27 to provision the environment and run baseline tests

Rishi (cc'd) can speak to dedicated capacity/rough timelines if you want that option. Connor will be our onboarding engineer for the trial.

If hosted works, we can stand up credentials and the eval harness within 48 hours of kickoff.

Subject: Dedicated sandbox and VPC notes

Hi Sam  quick tech note on the dedicated/VPC options so you can weigh them: 

- Dedicated sandbox: We reserve a small GPU pool (1-2 GPUs, same model family) for the trial. Provisioning typically takes 2-3 business days. Pros: predictable throughput and no noisy neighbors. Cons: higher cost and slightly slower start.
- VPC trial: For PHI/PCI/strict isolation we can deploy a private control plane into your VPC (we still manage the runtime). Provisioning is ~1 week and requires a network handoff (we'll share network-requirements.xlsx).

If your main gating items are network isolation and SOC-level auditability, choose VPC. If you just need to validate concurrency/throughput, choose dedicated sandbox. For quick baseline quality checks, hosted is fastest.

I'll be available on the kickoff once we pick an option  I'll also prepare a minimal traffic profile and a short load script for the throughput validation.
